correctness.rationale: All quantifiers concern one fixed finite graph with 16 labelled vertices and exactly 64 move repertoires. The two enumerators bijectively list 272 perfect matchings: least-unmatched recursion and reversed-even-parity-to-odd-neighbor injection. The 24 coordinate squares are complete (four for every axis pair). The two independently recomputed exact-integer graph algorithms, BFS using bitmask-flip adjacency and DSU using edge-set replacements, agree for every one of the 64 masks and reproduce the eleven component spectra; each spectrum partitions 272 and class multiplicities sum to 64. Under arbitrary strictly positive allowed RK plaquette coefficients, the positive semidefinite quadratic form vanishes exactly for component-constant vectors, proving the zero-mode degeneracy. No finite computation is extrapolated to larger dimension.

value.rationale: In a constrained quantum dimer model, disabling a coordinate-plane orientation is a natural anisotropy/control restriction; ergodicity and RK ground-space degeneracy are exact physically relevant outcomes. The four-cube is the first nontrivial binary cube with frozen isotropic square-flip states. The complete classification of all 64 physically distinct labelled control repertoires, reduced to 11 symmetry types, is a natural exhaustive classification, not an arbitrary small parameter slice. It establishes the sharp minimal orientation budget: all six are necessary to keep the known 264-state mobile sector connected, and removing one already splits it 198+32+32+1+1. RK zero-mode multiplicities are then exactly the new component counts for all positive selected flip coefficients. This fills a precise simulation/controllability gap, independent of larger-dimensional extrapolation.
